newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News-Sept 26.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News-Sept 26.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a bid to regain its competitive edge and to raise funds for a A$150 million upgrade of its in-flight entertainment facilities, Qantas Airways is urging the federal government to change the law to allow the airline to introduce gaming on its internationl services. Qantas believes it needs to introduce computerised blackjack, poker and slot games to remain competitive in key markets. Page 1.

In an important step towards the development of the national electricity market, New South Wales businesses which have annual power bills of more than A$2 million will be able to shop around for the best power deals from October 1. By mid-1998, almost half the A$4 billion a year New South Wales retail power market will be open to full competition. Page 1.

A discussion paper launched by the Australian Society of Certified Practising Accountants in Sydney yesterday, aimed at reducing tax evasion and making the tax system simpler and more equitable, called for a flat income tax rate, a negative income tax sysem to replace welfare payments, and a retail turnover tax. Page 5.

Ampolex Ltd has agreed to pay A$17.9 million to GPG Nominees Pty Ltd and County NatWest in a settlement of the long-standing legal battle over the conversion ratio of Ampolex's convertible notes, clearing the way for Mobil Corp to complete its A$1.8 billion takeover of the oil and gas group. Page 23.

BHP managing director John Prescott said yesterday that BHP would not introduce electric arc furnace technology to its Newcastle steel works because the cost of raw materials was too high. Prescott's comments came just one day after chairman Brian Loton told a shareholders meeting that the future of Newcastle steel-making was in doubt. Page 23.

Hudson Conway Ltd received more than A$40 million in fees and construction costs linked to the A$1.6 billion Crown casino project in 1995/96, according to the Crown Ltd annual report. Hudson Conway received a A$14.25 million project management fee and A$.6 million for construction employee services. Page 25.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Following the release of Transport Department figures showing the airline's international market share had dropped almost three percentage points in 1995/96, shares in Qantas Airways Ltd yesterday hit a new low, closing at A$1.86, three cents down on the previous day and four cents below its issue price of A$1.90 when the airline floated in August last year. Page 19.

After finalising a financing agreement for its huge Bluewater retail development in the United Kingdom, Lend Lease Corp Ltd has formed a joint venture with building materials group Blue Circle Industries Plc BCI.AX in a A$10 billion staged commercial and residential development of 940 hectares in north-west Kent. Page 19.

A partial settlement of the complex convertible notes litigation allowed United States oil and gas giant Mobil Corp to acquire most of the remaining Ampolex Ltd securities yesterday, moving it closer to 100 percent control. However, Ampolex has lost A$1.9 million after paying its share of the settlement with Guinness Peat Group and broker County NatWest Markets. Page 19.

Command Petroleum Ltd has requested that its shares be suspended from trade until October 1 while friendly merger negotiations continue. Industry analysts suggest Command's largest shareholder, US-based Snyder Oil Corp, is the likely seller of its 30 percent stake, thought to be worth A$100 million. Page 20.

Four conservation groups - the Wilderness Society, Environment Victoria, Friends of the Earth and the Native Forest Network - yesterday launched a consumer boycott of Amcor Ltd's fine-paper products, predominantly the Reflex brand of copy paper, because o its use of Victorian and Tasmanian native forest fibres. Page 21.

Although BHP chief executive John Prescott said yesterday that there was no evidence which "really goes against the due diligence", the company is reviewing the due diligence carried out on Magma Copper Co's assets before last December's A$3.2 billion takover in an effort to uncover reasons behind its current losses. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In line with its strategy of forming a global property development empire, Lend Lease Corp has joined with Blue Circle Industries in a A$10 billion venture to build a satellite city at the rail-link to the Channel Tunnel. The Eurocity will be located on he site where Lend Lease is constructing the A$1.4 billion Bluewater shopping and entertainment complex. Page 25.

After addressing an Australia-Israel Chamber of Commerce lunch in Sydney yesterday, BHP managing director John Prescott tried to play down concerns over the company's performance and strategy by stating that many of BHP's businesses were operationally strong and the second quarter had begun on a positive note. Page 25.

After Ampolex yesterday announced it would pay A$17.9 million to Guinness Peat Group and County NatWest, ending a 15-month court battle over Ampolex's convertible notes, Mobil Corp declared it had acquired 5.6 million Ampolex convertible notes, bringing is holding to 97 percent. Page 27.

Crown Casino chairman Lloyd Williams said the casino would actively seek to build on its significant revenues from international high rollers after figures released yesterday in the annual report revealed 30 percent of Crown's A$490 million of gaming revenues in the year to June 30 were attributable to international players. Page 27.

Australian life insurer National Mutual Holdings is now offering policies on the Internet. Customers will be able to activate an accidental death policy without any other contact with the company, just by pressing the send button on the Internet. Page 27.

Australian National Industries director Peter Joseph yesterday defended the board's move to depose directors Ross Palmer and Fred Smith as Palmer responded by putting forward a resolution to remove Joseph as a director at the company's annual general meeting. Page 27.
THE AGE

Lend Lease Corp yesterday announced a A$10 billion joint venture with Blue Circle Industries to build a satellite city at the rail-link to the Channel Tunnel. The Eurocity project is located on the UK partner's southern Kent site where Lend Lease recentl began construction on its A$1.4 billion Bluewater shopping and entertainment complex. Page B1.

While endorsing the government's emphasis on restoring the gudget to a surplus, former Reserve Bank governor Bernie Fraser yesterday warned that unless falling unemployment and rising living standards were delivered, the Coalition would lose public support for low inflation and sound public finances. Page B1.

National Mutual Holdings has become the first Australian life insurer to offer policies on the Internet, spending about A$200,000 on designing its home page, which allows customers to activate an accidental death policy without any other contact with the company. Page B2.

The Australian Society of Certified Practising Accountants has recommended a standard across-the-board tax rate of 20 percent for firms and individuals and an indirect retail tax regime in a discussion paper, A Tax System For the 21st Century, designed to generate debate about tax in Australia. Page B2.

Food ingredients group Burns Philp & Co yesterday announced it had singed a letter of intent to buy British food preservative company Aplin & Barrett from Applied Microbiology Inc in a deal comprising a cash payment of A$17.2 million and the return to AMI of 2.42 million AMBI shares owned by Burns Philp. Page B2.

Command Petroleum yesterday asked for its shares to be suspended while it conducts merger talks with an undisclosed party. Expected to make an announcement next week, Command managing director John Doran ruled out the possibility of major shareholder Snyder Oil increasing its 33 percent holding. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
